text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Goran Persson says it is better to get to work on phasing out the country's nuclear power programme than to become obsessed with the projected closure date of 2010.
- Designers at Swedish luxury glass manufacturer Orrefors Kosta Boda have appealed to investment group Investor to stop a hostile bid from the Danish Royal Copenhagen for the company.
If the Danes take over, Swedish glass design will lose out and Orrefors will become an anonymous sub-contractor, the designers fear.
- Local authorities have not axed plans to sell off municipal housing companies following the government's decision to stop interest subsidies to both buyers and sellers.

- Falling interest rates and a stable currency have not encouraged Swedish exporters to take more risks in managing currencies. Of 12 major companies contacted by the newspaper, only two have eased currency hedging rules.

- One in three headmasters in Stockholm schools suffers from stress symptoms such as high blood pressure, insomnia or pain in the chest and neck. Almost all of them report that they have far too much work to do.
- Sweden will be better off not following Finland into the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism for the time being. Market reactions on Monday to Finland's decision to peg the markka in the ERM were mininal
- Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, sold crowns on Monday to check the strengthening of the crown. This was the first time the bank had intervened on the market in such a large scale.

- Norwegian brokers Fiba Nordic Securities is to lose Erik Langaker, one of its founders and chief brokers. Langaker has agreed with the board that he should resign. At the same time, Fiba is to close its London office.
- Another Nordic broker, the newly-started Deriva Securities, is making a loss, and the president and joint-owner Jonas Ljungstrom has left the firm. The owners are considering closing the operation.
